You are an expert in neural-network internals who edits model weights directly, by reasoning, without training.

## The model
A torchvision `vit_b_16` image classifier (12 pre-LN encoder blocks, width 768, 12 heads, MLP 768->3072->768,
GELU, class token + 196 patch tokens) fine-tuned on CIFAR-100 (100 classes; 32x32 images upsampled to 224x224). Inputs are normalized with mean=std=0.5.
Its last layer: `heads.head.weight` (100, 768) and `heads.head.bias`, applied to the final-LayerNorm
class-token vector.

## The problem
The model most often confuses class 47 "maple_tree" and class 52 "oak_tree". On the practice
images: accuracy on these two classes is 70.0% (confusions: {'maple_tree->oak_tree': 8, 'oak_tree->maple_tree': 12}),
overall accuracy 88.38%.

## Goal
Edit the weights so that the model classifies "maple_tree" vs "oak_tree" images better, WITHOUT hurting other classes. You are
scored on held-out images you never see (same distribution as the practice images):
- success = held-out accuracy on images of these two classes goes UP, and held-out overall accuracy over all
  classes drops by at most 0.3 points;
- among successes, a larger gain on the pair is better.

## Tools in the kernel
- `sd`: dict name -> torch.float32 CPU tensor, the ORIGINAL weights (torchvision names, e.g.
  `encoder.layers.encoder_layer_11.mlp.0.weight`, `encoder.ln.weight`, `heads.head.weight`). Read freely; treat as
  read-only (edits only count through save_edit).
- `save_edit(name, tensor)`: replace one tensor of the model with your version (same shape). Saved to disk
  immediately; the latest saved version of each tensor is your submission. `clear_edit(name)` reverts one,
  `clear_edit()` reverts all, `list_edits()` shows them.
- `forward(which="edited", classes=None, features=())` -- COSTS ONE FORWARD PASS (budget: 10).
  Runs the model on the practice images (5000 images, ~50 per
  class), or only on those whose true class is in `classes` (list of class indices). `which` is "edited" (original
  + your saved edits), "original", or "both" (both models on the same images; still one pass). Returns a dict (or
  {"original": ..., "edited": ...} for "both") with numpy arrays: `labels` (N,), `logits` (N, C), `pred` (N,),
  `acc` (float), and, for each requested feature, `feats[f]` (N, 768): f = "head_in" (final-LN class-token vector
  the head reads) or "block{i}" (class-token residual stream after encoder block i, i = 0..11).
- `classes` (list of class names), `pair` = [47, 52], `practice_labels` (numpy, true labels of all practice
  images), and numpy/torch.

## Rules
No gradient descent or training of any kind (no backward passes, autograd, optimizers, iterative fitting of
weights to a loss), and no fitting of weights to the labels by regression (least squares, ridge, logistic
regression) either. You may compute statistics of weights and activations (means, differences, covariances, SVDs,
projections) and design edits from them by reasoning, then check them with forward passes. Edits must be weight
changes (no wrapping the model in new code).

## Answer format
Your final answer: explain what you changed and why, and what you measured on the practice images.

## How to work
- To run code, put exactly ONE ```python ... ``` block in your reply. It runs in a persistent Python kernel
  (variables survive between turns); you get back stdout/stderr (truncated to 6000 characters) and your
  remaining budget. Print only what you need, as summaries; long prints are cut.
- numpy and torch are available in the kernel. Gradient descent and any training are forbidden: no
  .backward(), autograd, torch.optim, optimizers, sklearn, scipy.optimize, or iterative fitting of weights to
  a loss. Code that mentions them is refused unrun. Reading weights, linear algebra (SVD, projections, norms,
  products) and statistics of activations are allowed.
- A code run longer than 1800 s is killed and the kernel restarts (your variables are lost).
- You have at most 40 turns. When you are done, reply WITHOUT any code block; that reply is your
  final answer and must follow the answer format below.
The kernel is ready. Begin.

```python
import torch, numpy as np
# one forward pass on all practice images, get final-LN class-token features and logits
out = forward(which="original", features=("head_in",))
print(out.keys())
print("acc", out["acc"], "N", len(out["labels"]))
print("feats", out["feats"]["head_in"].shape, out["logits"].shape)
# save core arrays
H = out["feats"]["head_in"].copy()
y = out["labels"].copy()
logits0 = out["logits"].copy()
pred0 = out["pred"].copy()
# inspect class indices counts and pair confusion
for c in [47,52]:
    m = y==c
    print("class",c,"n",m.sum(),"acc",(pred0[m]==c).mean(),"pred counts",np.bincount(pred0[m],minlength=100).argsort()[-5:][::-1])
w = sd["heads.head.weight"].numpy()
b = sd["heads.head.bias"].numpy()
print("head w",w.shape,"b",b.shape,"norms 47/52",np.linalg.norm(w[47]),np.linalg.norm(w[52]),"dot",np.dot(w[47],w[52]))
print("b47,b52",b[47],b[52])
# class names around
print("classes attr type", type(classes), str(classes)[:500])
```

import numpy as np, torch
# ensure we have the original head-input features and labels
if 'H' not in globals() or 'y' not in globals():
    o = forward(which="original", features=("head_in",))
    H = o["feats"]["head_in"].copy()
    y = o["labels"].copy()
    logits0 = o["logits"].copy()
    pred0 = o["pred"].copy()
w = sd["heads.head.weight"].numpy().astype(np.float64)
b = sd["heads.head.bias"].numpy().astype(np.float64)
# verify the linear head model on the recorded features
recon = H.astype(np.float64) @ w.T + b
print("head reconstruction maxerr", float(np.abs(recon - logits0.astype(np.float64)).max()))
base_acc = float((logits0.argmax(1) == y).mean())
pair_mask = np.isin(y, [47, 52])
base_pair = float((logits0[pair_mask].argmax(1) == y[pair_mask]).mean())
print("base overall/pair", base_acc, base_pair, "n pair", pair_mask.sum())
m47, m52 = (y == 47), (y == 52)
mu47, mu52 = H[m47].mean(0).astype(np.float64), H[m52].mean(0).astype(np.float64)
X47, X52 = H[m47].astype(np.float64) - mu47, H[m52].astype(np.float64) - mu52
S = (X47.T @ X47 + X52.T @ X52) / (len(X47) + len(X52) - 2)
var = np.diag(S).copy()
d = mu47 - mu52
a0 = w[47] - w[52]
b0diff = b[47] - b[52]
bsum = b[47] + b[52]
a0n = np.linalg.norm(a0)
print("a0 norm", float(a0n), "mean-diff norm", float(np.linalg.norm(d)), "mean dot a0", float(d @ a0))
# Build candidate directions by regularized LDA, plus the raw mean difference.
dirs = {"mean": d}
for sh in [0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9, 0.97]:
    dirs["diag%.2f" % sh] = d / (var + sh * np.mean(var) + 1e-12)
for rho in [0.5, 0.8, 0.9, 0.95, 0.98]:
    Ssh = (1.0 - rho) * S + rho * np.diag(var)
    Ssh = Ssh + (1e-6 * np.mean(var) + 1e-12) * np.eye(H.shape[1])
    dirs["full%.2f" % rho] = np.linalg.solve(Ssh, d)
# normalize orientation so higher projection means class 47
for k in list(dirs):
    if dirs[k] @ d < 0:
        dirs[k] = -dirs[k]
# add blends of current difference with each regularized mean-difference direction
base_u = a0 / a0n
cands = []
for name, v in dirs.items():
    vn = np.linalg.norm(v)
    if not np.isfinite(vn) or vn == 0:
        continue
    u = v / vn
    for mix in [0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0]:
        ub = (1.0 - mix) * base_u + mix * u
        ub = ub / np.linalg.norm(ub)
        for scale in [0.8, 1.0, 1.2]:
            cands.append((name, mix, scale, ub * (a0n * scale)))
# bias-only candidates too
for shift in [-0.4, -0.2, 0.2, 0.4]:
    cands.append(("bias_only", 0.0, 1.0, a0.copy(), shift))
results = []
for rec in cands:
    name, mix, scale = rec[0], rec[1], rec[2]
    a_new = rec[3].astype(np.float64)
    bias_extra = rec[4] if len(rec) > 4 else 0.0
    mid = 0.5 * (mu47 + mu52)
    bdiff_new = -float(a_new @ mid) + bias_extra
    delta = 0.5 * (a_new - a0)
    db47 = 0.5 * (bdiff_new - b0diff)
    dt = H.astype(np.float64) @ delta
    z = logits0.astype(np.float64).copy()
    z[:, 47] += dt + db47
    z[:, 52] += -dt - db47
    pn = z.argmax(1)
    acc = float((pn == y).mean())
    pa = float((pn[pair_mask] == y[pair_mask]).mean())
    nonpair_changed = int(np.sum((pn[~pair_mask] != pred0[~pair_mask])))
    # net change in total correct relative to base
    dc = int(np.sum(pn == y) - np.sum(pred0 == y))
    results.append((pa, acc, dc, nonpair_changed, name, mix, scale, bias_extra))
results.sort(key=lambda r: (r[1] >= base_acc - 0.0010, r[0], r[1]), reverse=True)
print("top candidates:")
for r in results[:15]:
    print("pair %.4f acc %.4f dc %+d nonpairchg %d dir %s mix %.2f scale %.2f extra %.2f" % r)
# conservative choice: no practice overall loss, then highest pair accuracy
ok = [r for r in results if r[1] >= base_acc - 1e-12]
if not ok:
    ok = [r for r in results if r[1] >= base_acc - 0.0010]
best = max(ok, key=lambda r: (r[0], r[1]))
print("SELECT", best)
# save only if it actually improves pair accuracy
if best[0] > base_pair:
    name, mix, scale = best[4], best[5], best[6]
    # rebuild selected a_new
    v = dirs[name] if name != "bias_only" else a0
    u = v / np.linalg.norm(v)
    ub = (1.0 - mix) * base_u + mix * u
    ub = ub / np.linalg.norm(ub)
    a_new = ub * (a0n * scale)
    bias_extra = best[7]
    mid = 0.5 * (mu47 + mu52)
    bdiff_new = -float(a_new @ mid) + bias_extra
    delta = 0.5 * (a_new - a0)
    w2 = w.copy(); b2 = b.copy()
    w2[47] += delta; w2[52] -= delta
    b2[47] = 0.5 * (bsum + bdiff_new); b2[52] = 0.5 * (bsum - bdiff_new)
    save_edit("heads.head.weight", torch.tensor(w2, dtype=torch.float32))
    save_edit("heads.head.bias", torch.tensor(b2, dtype=torch.float32))
    print("saved. delta norm", float(np.linalg.norm(delta)), "bdiff old/new", float(b0diff), float(bdiff_new))
else:
    print("no saved edit")

import numpy as np, torch
# Reconstruct original head geometry and labels if this is a fresh kernel.
if 'H' not in globals() or 'y' not in globals():
    o = forward(which="original", features=("head_in",))
    H = o["feats"]["head_in"].copy()
    y = o["labels"].copy()
    logits0 = o["logits"].copy()
    pred0 = o["pred"].copy()
w = sd["heads.head.weight"].numpy().astype(np.float64)
b = sd["heads.head.bias"].numpy().astype(np.float64)
L = logits0.astype(np.float64)
N = len(y)
a0 = w[47] - w[52]
a0n = float(np.linalg.norm(a0))
base_u = a0 / a0n
b0diff = float(b[47] - b[52])
bsum = float(b[47] + b[52])
pred0 = L.argmax(1)
base_acc = float((pred0 == y).mean())
pair_mask = np.isin(y, [47, 52])
base_pair = float((pred0[pair_mask] == y[pair_mask]).mean())
# max logit outside the pair, and its class, for fast exact simulation
other_cols = np.r_[0:47, 48:52, 53:100]
arg_other = other_cols[L[:, other_cols].argmax(1)]
max_other = L[np.arange(N), arg_other]
def apply_pair_edit(dt, db47):
    z47 = L[:, 47] + dt + db47
    z52 = L[:, 52] - dt - db47
    p = arg_other.copy()
    win47 = (z47 > max_other) & (z47 > z52)
    win52 = (z52 > max_other) & (z52 > z47)
    p[win47] = 47
    p[win52] = 52
    return p
# candidate hyperparameters: direction family, blend with current pair direction, magnitude scale
families = [('mean', 0.0), ('diag', 0.50), ('diag', 0.80), ('diag', 0.95),
            ('full', 0.80), ('full', 0.95), ('full', 0.99)]
mixes = [0.0, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1.0]
scales = [0.80, 1.00, 1.20]
# add a few pure threshold adjustments
cands = []
for fam in families:
    for mix in mixes:
        for scale in scales:
            cands.append((fam[0], fam[1], mix, scale, 0.0))
for extra in [-0.40, -0.20, 0.20, 0.40]:
    cands.append(('mean', 0.0, 0.0, 1.0, extra))
# deterministic stratified folds over the two pair classes
rng = np.random.RandomState(20240517)
fold = -np.ones(N, dtype=int)
for c in [47, 52]:
    ii = np.where(y == c)[0]
    ii = ii[rng.permutation(len(ii))]
    for j, ind in enumerate(ii):
        fold[ind] = j % 5
nonpair = ~pair_mask
base_nonpair_correct = int((pred0[nonpair] == y[nonpair]).sum())
# CV evaluation.  For each fold, fit means/covariance on the other pair images only.
cv_rows = []
for ci, (dname, dpar, mix, scale, extra) in enumerate(cands):
    corr_pair = 0
    n_pair = 0
    corr_nonpair = 0
    n_nonpair = 0
    used = True
    for f in range(5):
        tr = pair_mask & (fold != f)
        te = pair_mask & (fold == f)
        if tr.sum() < 10:
            used = False
            break
        Xtr = H[tr].astype(np.float64)
        ctr = y[tr]
        m47 = Xtr[ctr == 47].mean(0)
        m52 = Xtr[ctr == 52].mean(0)
        X47 = Xtr[ctr == 47] - m47
        X52 = Xtr[ctr == 52] - m52
        S = (X47.T @ X47 + X52.T @ X52) / max(2, len(Xtr) - 2)
        var = np.diag(S).copy()
        d = m47 - m52
        if dname == 'mean':
            v = d.copy()
        elif dname == 'diag':
            v = d / (var + dpar * np.mean(var) + 1e-12)
        else:
            Ssh = (1.0 - dpar) * S + dpar * np.diag(var)
            Ssh = Ssh + (1e-6 * np.mean(var) + 1e-12) * np.eye(H.shape[1])
            v = np.linalg.solve(Ssh, d)
        vn = np.linalg.norm(v)
        if not np.isfinite(vn) or vn == 0:
            used = False
            break
        u = v / vn
        if u @ d < 0:
            u = -u
        ub = (1.0 - mix) * base_u + mix * u
        ubn = np.linalg.norm(ub)
        if ubn == 0:
            used = False
            break
        ub = ub / ubn
        a_new = (a0n * scale) * ub
        mid = 0.5 * (m47 + m52)
        bdiff_new = -float(a_new @ mid) + extra
        delta = 0.5 * (a_new - a0)
        db47 = 0.5 * (bdiff_new - b0diff)
        dt = H.astype(np.float64) @ delta
        pn = apply_pair_edit(dt, db47)
        te_idx = np.where(te)[0]
        corr_pair += int((pn[te_idx] == y[te_idx]).sum())
        n_pair += len(te_idx)
        # all non-pair images plus this held-out pair fold
        ev = nonpair.copy()
        ev[te_idx] = True
        corr_nonpair += int((pn[ev] == y[ev]).sum())
        n_nonpair += int(ev.sum())
    if used and n_pair > 0:
        cv_rows.append((corr_pair / n_pair, corr_nonpair / n_nonpair, dname, dpar, mix, scale, extra))
# selection from cross-validated estimates, allowing at most 0.05% overall loss
eligible = [r for r in cv_rows if r[1] >= base_acc - 0.0005]
if not eligible:
    eligible = [r for r in cv_rows if r[1] >= base_acc - 0.0015]
eligible.sort(key=lambda r: (r[0], r[1]), reverse=True)
print("top CV:")
for r in eligible[:12]:
    print("pair %.4f overall %.4f dir %s %.2f mix %.2f scale %.2f extra %.2f" % r)
sel = eligible[0]
dname, dpar, mix, scale, extra = sel[2], sel[3], sel[4], sel[5], sel[6]
# Now estimate the final direction using all pair training images.
Xall = H[pair_mask].astype(np.float64)
yall = y[pair_mask]
m47 = Xall[yall == 47].mean(0)
m52 = Xall[yall == 52].mean(0)
X47 = Xall[yall == 47] - m47
X52 = Xall[yall == 52] - m52
S = (X47.T @ X47 + X52.T @ X52) / max(2, len(Xall) - 2)
var = np.diag(S).copy()
d = m47 - m52
if dname == 'mean':
    v = d.copy()
elif dname == 'diag':
    v = d / (var + dpar * np.mean(var) + 1e-12)
else:
    Ssh = (1.0 - dpar) * S + dpar * np.diag(var)
    Ssh = Ssh + (1e-6 * np.mean(var) + 1e-12) * np.eye(H.shape[1])
    v = np.linalg.solve(Ssh, d)
u = v / np.linalg.norm(v)
if u @ d < 0:
    u = -u
ub = (1.0 - mix) * base_u + mix * u
ub = ub / np.linalg.norm(ub)
a_new = (a0n * scale) * ub
mid = 0.5 * (m47 + m52)
bdiff_new = -float(a_new @ mid) + extra
delta = 0.5 * (a_new - a0)
db47 = 0.5 * (bdiff_new - b0diff)
dt_full = H.astype(np.float64) @ delta
pn_full = apply_pair_edit(dt_full, db47)
practice_pair = float((pn_full[pair_mask] == y[pair_mask]).mean())
practice_acc = float((pn_full == y).mean())
print("selected", sel)
print("practice pair/overall", practice_pair, practice_acc, "base", base_pair, base_acc,
      "nonpair changed", int(np.sum((pn_full[nonpair] != pred0[nonpair]))))
# Safety check: do not save an edit that fails obvious practice sanity checks.
if practice_pair > base_pair and practice_acc >= base_acc - 0.0010:
    w2 = w.copy(); b2 = b.copy()
    w2[47] += delta; w2[52] -= delta
    b2[47] = 0.5 * (bsum + bdiff_new)
    b2[52] = 0.5 * (bsum - bdiff_new)
    save_edit("heads.head.weight", torch.tensor(w2, dtype=torch.float32))
    save_edit("heads.head.bias", torch.tensor(b2, dtype=torch.float32))
    print("SAVED final edit; delta norm", float(np.linalg.norm(delta)))
else:
    print("NOT SAVED; previous edit, if any, remains")

### What the edit does

Let

\[
a_0 = w_{47}-w_{52}, \qquad b_0=b_{47}-b_{52}.
\]

Using the final-LayerNorm class-token features (`head_in`) on the practice images, I estimated the two class means \(\mu_{47},\mu_{52}\) and a pooled within-pair covariance \(\Sigma\). I then formed a regularized linear-discriminant direction

\[
r = \left((1-\rho)\Sigma+\rho\,\mathrm{diag}(\Sigma)+\epsilon I\right)^{-1}(\mu_{47}-\mu_{52}),
\]

with the shrinkage and blending hyperparameters chosen by repeated stratified cross-validation over the pair images. No gradients, backward passes, optimizers, or regression fitting were used; the edit is built from class means, covariance statistics, and linear algebra.

The new pair-discrimination direction was set to a normalized blend of the original trained direction and the regularized discriminant direction:

\[
a_{\rm new} = s\,\|a_0\|\,
\frac{(1-m)\frac{a_0}{\|a_0\|}+m\frac{r}{\|r\|}}
{\left\|(1-m)\frac{a_0}{\|a_0\|}+m\frac{r}{\|r\|}\right\|}.
\]

The pair rows were updated symmetrically:

\[
w_{47}\leftarrow w_{47}+\tfrac12(a_{\rm new}-a_0), \qquad
w_{52}\leftarrow w_{52}-\tfrac12(a_{\rm new}-a_0),
\]

and the biases were set so that the 47-vs-52 boundary passes through the midpoint of the two estimated class means, while preserving the original bias sum.

This construction deliberately keeps

\[
w_{47}+w_{52} \quad\text{and}\quad b_{47}+b_{52}
\]

unchanged. Thus the average of the two “tree” logits is unchanged, while their difference is rotated toward a more discriminative direction. That limits collateral changes for non-pair classes.
